evals.prompt: I attached screenshots of a fintech mobile app. When I scroll, the yellow header turns into a search bar, cards stack while scrolling, and Pesos/Dolares/Reservas tabs slide smoothly. What are these called and how do I prompt Codex to build them in Next.js?
evals.expected_output: Names the patterns as collapsing header/morphing search bar, sticky card stack, and animated segmented control/pager; explains start/transition/end states; gives a Next.js/Tailwind/Framer Motion prompt and QA checklist.

evals.prompt: Build me a React Native Expo screen for a finance dashboard with MercadoPago-style scrolling header, swipe tabs, and promo card pile. I want real code, not just explanation.
evals.expected_output: Produces a component plan and React Native/Reanimated-oriented implementation using SafeArea, scroll shared values, interpolated header/search styles, segmented tabs or pager, and a card stack; includes accessibility and reduced-motion notes.

evals.prompt: Audit my mobile CRM PWA UI. It looks generic AI generated. Make it feel like a real premium internal tool without adding random glassmorphism.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses generic UI issues, chooses a coherent internal-tool visual direction, defines tokens, layout hierarchy, component/state improvements, and avoids generic purple gradients/glassmorphism/random decoration.

evals.prompt: I need a reusable prompt for Claude Code to implement sticky stacked cards in an existing Next.js page without breaking scroll performance.
evals.expected_output: Gives a copy-paste prompt describing sticky card stack mechanics, CSS sticky top offsets, z-index, overlap, transform/opacity performance, reduced motion, and integration constraints for existing code.
